name: Semantic Coherence Graph Analysis
description: Examines the continuity of ideas by plotting sentence-level meanings on a mathematical graph. Large Language Models are designed to predict the most statistically probable next words, which naturally forces their ideas to flow in a hyper-logical, extremely smooth sequence. Human writing, conversely, exhibits 'semantic jumps'—sudden shifts in focus, tangential thought inserts, or cognitive leaps that break the linear flow. This algorithm measures how 'perfectly' the sentences transition from one to the next.
algorithm: Sentence-Level Embedding and Local Coherence Modeling
mechanism: The system processes the text by converting every sentence into a high-dimensional vector (embedding) using models like Sentence-BERT. It then constructs a 'Semantic Graph' where nodes are sentences and edges represent the cosine similarity (meaning-closeness) between adjacent nodes. The algorithm calculates the variance in edge weights throughout the graph. AI-generated text produces a graph with consistently high edge weights (indicating that every sentence is very semantically similar to the one before it). Human text produces a 'bumpier' graph with higher variance, reflecting natural conversational leaps and bounds.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing deep investigative journalism, personal narratives, and complex argumentative essays where human cognitive shifts are normally abundant.
strengths:
• Excellent at detecting text where the AI has 'hallucinated' excessive padding just to connect two distant ideas smoothly.
• Highly resilient against simple word replacement (synonym substitution) because it measures the underlying meaning of the whole sentence.
limitations:
• Computationally expensive compared to basic statistical methods due to the need for deep neural embeddings layer processing.
• Can trigger false positives on highly structured, step-by-step instructional writing or dry technical specifications.
parameters:
Analysis: Sentence-BERT Embedding Cosine Similarity Graphing
Metric: Local Coherence Edge Variance and Flow Predictability
Output: 0-100 Semantic Smoothness (Artificial Coherence) Score
accuracy: High — 82-89% accuracy. One of the most robust semantic detection methods available, especially when paired with Syntactic Tree Depth analysis.

references.title: Barzilay, R. & Lapata, M. (2008). Modeling Local Coherence: An Entity-Based Approach. Computational Linguistics.
Foltz, P.W. et al. (1998). The Measurement of Textual Coherence with Latent Semantic Analysis. Discourse Processes.
